When ʿAbd al-Muttalib made his camel rise, a spring of sweet water burst out from under its hoof. ʿAbd al-Muttalib said “Allahu akbar”, and his companions said it too. He dismounted and drank, and his companions drank, and they filled their water-skins. Then he called the clans of Quraysh, who had been watching all of this: “Come to the water, for Allah has given us water.” They came and drank and filled their water-skins.

text: All of them. Then they said: “By Allah, the judgement has been given for you against us. By Allah, we will never dispute with you over Zamzam. The One who gave you this water in this desert is the One who gave you Zamzam. Go back to your watering of the pilgrims, rightly guided.” He went back and they went back with him. They never reached the soothsayer, and they left him and Zamzam alone.

text: Al-Umawi adds that ʿAbd al-Muttalib found the colony of the ants and the crow pecking beside it, between two idols of Quraysh. Quraysh objected to his digging there; he told his son al-Harith to keep them back, and when they saw he would not give up, they left him to dig. As he dug deeper he found two gazelles of gold that Jurhum had buried, with swords and coats of armour.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Then Abraha built al-Qullays in Sanaʿa, a church whose like had not been seen anywhere on earth in its time, and he wrote to the Negus: “I have built for you a church like none ever built for a king before you, and I will not stop until I have turned the pilgrimage of the Arabs to it.”

text: When the Arabs spoke of Abraha’s letter to the Negus, a man of Kinanah was angered. He went to al-Qullays and showed his contempt for it, then went back to his own land. Abraha was told that a man from the people of the House in Makkah had done this when he heard of Abraha’s plan to turn the pilgrimage away from it. Abraha was enraged, and swore that he would march on the House and destroy it.

text: Then he ordered the Abyssinians to prepare, and they made ready. He set out, taking the elephant with him. The Arabs heard of it and were horrified, and they saw it as their duty to fight him when they heard that he meant to destroy the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House of Allah. A man of the nobles and kings of Yemen called Dhu Nafr called his people and other Arabs to fight Abraha and defend the Sacred House. He met him in battle, but Dhu Nafr and his men were defeated, and Dhu Nafr was taken captive.

text: When Abraha reached the land of Khathʿam, Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khathʿami came against him with the two tribes of Khathʿam and the Arabs who followed him. Abraha defeated him and took him captive. When he meant to kill him, Nufayl said: “O king, do not kill me, for I will be your guide in the land of the Arabs.” So Abraha let him go.

text: He took him along as his guide. When he passed by al-Taʾif, Masʿud ibn Muʿattib came out to him with men of Thaqif and said: “O king, we will not oppose you. This house of ours is not the House you want. You want the House in Makkah, and we will send someone with you to guide you to it.” They sent Abu Righal with him to show him the way to Makkah. Abraha set out with Abu Righal until he brought him to al-Mughammas.

text: When Abraha camped at al-Mughammas, he sent an Abyssinian called al-Aswad ibn Mafsud with horsemen to Makkah. He drove off to Abraha the wealth of the people of Tihama, from Quraysh and others, and among it were two hundred camels of ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, who was then the eldest and leader of Quraysh. Quraysh, Kinanah, Hudhayl and the others in the Haram thought of fighting him; then they knew they had no power to fight him, and they left it.

text: Abraha sent Hunata al-Himyari to Makkah and told him: “Ask for the leader and noblest man of this land and tell him: The king says, I have not come to fight you. I have come only to destroy this House. If you do not stand against us to defend it, I have no need of your blood.” When Hunata entered Makkah he asked for the leader of Quraysh, and was told: ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. He went to him and told him what Abraha had said. ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “By Allah, we do not want to fight him, and we have no power to do so. This is the Sacred House of Allah and the house of His Khalil Ibrahim, peace be upon him. If He protects it from him, it is His Sanctuary and His House; and if He leaves it to him, by Allah, we have no way to defend it.”

He asked for Dhu Nafr, who was his friend, and went in to him in his prison. Dhu Nafr said: “What help can a captive be, who expects the king to kill him morning or evening? But Unays, the keeper of the elephant, is my friend. I will send for him, commend you to him, and ask him to get you leave to see the king.” Unays spoke to Abraha: “O king, the leader of Quraysh is at your door asking to see you. He is the master of the well of Makkah, who feeds people in the plain and the wild animals on the mountain tops.” Abraha gave him leave.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib was the most handsome and dignified of men. When Abraha saw him he honoured him, and he would not seat him below himself, nor let the Abyssinians see him seat him on his throne. So he came down from his throne and sat on his carpet, and seated ʿAbd al-Muttalib beside him. He said to his interpreter: “Ask him what he needs.” ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “My need is that the king return to me two hundred camels he has taken from me.” Abraha said to his interpreter: “Tell him: I admired you when I saw you, but I think less of you now that you have spoken. You speak to me about two hundred camels I took from you, and say nothing of a House that is your religion and the religion of your fathers, which I have come to destroy?” ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.” Abraha said: “He will not protect it from me.” He said: “That is between you and Him.” And Abraha returned his camels to him.

Then ʿAbd al-Muttalib stood and took hold of the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah, and a group of Quraysh stood with him, calling on Allah and asking Him for help against Abraha and his army.

text: In the morning Abraha prepared to enter Makkah. He made his elephant ready and drew up his army; the elephant’s name was Mahmud. When they turned the elephant towards Makkah, Nufayl ibn Habib came and stood beside it, took hold of its ear and said: “Kneel, Mahmud, and go back safely to where you came from, for you are in the Sacred Land of Allah.” And he let go of its ear. The elephant knelt. Nufayl ran off and climbed the mountain. They beat the elephant to make it stand, but it refused. They turned it back towards Yemen, and it got up and hurried off. They turned it towards al-Sham and it did the same, and towards the east and it did the same. They turned it towards Makkah, and it knelt.
